title: What AI quietly broke in my engineering team

scenes.narration: Everyone expected AI to triple our velocity. So did I. It didn't, and I burned out asking what was wrong with my team.
Wrong question. AI made our code cheap, but it took away three things that held the team together.
First, the cost of building. It forced us to choose. Now every idea arrives as a working demo, and the bottleneck moves to whoever decides.
Second, the ladder of experience. AI lifts juniors the most, and confidence starts beating experience. Seniors fix the damage later.
Third, asking each other. Every "can you look at this?" made someone feel needed. Now the question goes to a chat window.
A hundred engineers chatting with the same model are not a hundred perspectives. They may be closer to one.
None of this shows up on a velocity chart. The full field notes are on my blog.
